name: Unique-Midpoint Core and Square Remainder
statement: For rooted-pair constraints $(w;\{u,v\})$ on a finite set $V$, call nonempty $W\subseteq V$ a core when every $w\in W$ roots a constraint whose two heads lie in $W$. An order satisfying $u\prec w$ or $v\prec w$ for every constraint exists exactly when no core exists. Repeatedly deleting a root with no constraint whose two heads remain computes the unique largest core; if it empties, the deletion order satisfies all constraints. Applied to unique-midpoint constraints of an isometric cube family $H$, a nonempty core proves $H$ nonpeelable. If the core is empty, only full-square constraints remain: an order peels exactly when it satisfies every unique-midpoint constraint and its first two vertices in every square are adjacent. Square constraints alone never obstruct elimination; any order nondecreasing in cube distance from a fixed cube vertex satisfies them. Hence a family with no unique-midpoint constraints is peelable.
proof: In any order, the first vertex of a core violates the constraint witnessing it. Conversely, unions of cores are cores, so iterative pruning leaves the unique largest one; when it is empty, every deleted root has an already deleted head and the deletion order satisfies all rooted-pair constraints. A distance-two pair has either one common neighbour, giving exactly such a constraint, or two common neighbours forming a square. The two square diagonals are both satisfied precisely when the first two square vertices are adjacent. Finally, relative to any fixed cube vertex, a square has one nearest vertex, two adjacent next-nearest vertices, and one farthest vertex, so every distance-nondecreasing order satisfies all square conditions. The metric elimination criterion translates the resulting orders into peelings.
comments: The core is a constructive sufficient obstruction. Its emptiness is not sufficient for peelability when full squares are present; the manuscript supplies a certified ample forbidden pc-minor with empty core.
